headline: Second day off the trail, still no run logged. Absorption is taking longer than a single day — which is exactly right after three back-to-back ultra days. Watch for the first easy run to tell the real recovery story.
confidence_reasons: Limited data sources active in last 3 days
confidence_attention: Limited data sources active in last 3 days

sections.overview: The picture right now is a system still digesting a very large meal. The crossing loaded an enormous chunk of running volume in a compressed window, and the two days since have been quiet on foot — that's the correct move, not a stall. Strength hasn't re-entered the log yet, which was one of yesterday's markers to watch and remains open; its return will be the clearest sign normal rhythm has resumed. Steps stay genuinely high even on the down days, so background load hasn't dropped to zero — the athlete isn't sitting still, just not running. The Polar "detraining" status is a mechanical artefact of a couple of low-run days against a big rolling average, not a real fitness signal, and shouldn't be read as anything more. Sleep across the block was short and broken, and whether it consolidates now is the other thread still hanging.
sections.trends: Zoom out and the shape is coherent: recent four-week volume roughly doubled over the prior block, driven almost entirely by the crossing rather than a gradual ramp, so this is a spike within a long consistent base rather than a sustainable new baseline. Year-to-date distance sits far ahead of the same point last year, which reframes the current quiet days — this isn't a fragile athlete easing off, it's someone with a deep accumulated base taking a well-earned trough. That trough is expected and healthy after an effort of this size; the trend only becomes a question if the quiet stretch runs longer than absorption should reasonably need.
sections.threshold: Threshold pace and its associated HR haven't moved — the last measurement is over a month old and predates the entire trail block, so there's simply no new data to reinterpret. Nothing in the crossing would sharpen threshold anyway; those were controlled low-HR durability days, not intensity work. The aerobic engine demonstrated its shape by holding form across three ultra days, but that's a durability signal, not a threshold one. Expect no threshold read until faster running re-enters and a fresh test lands.
sections.zones: Every trail day sat almost entirely in Z1 with only trace minutes drifting up — the intensity distribution across the block was about as polarised-toward-easy as it gets, which is exactly the intent for back-to-back ultra durability. There's no grey-zone problem here; if anything the block was deliberately submaximal throughout, controlled by HR rather than pace. What's absent is any Z3–Z5 stimulus, which is fine given the block's purpose but worth noting as the thing that'll need to return once absorption completes to keep the speed side of the ledger honest.
sections.hr_comparison: No new strength HR to read — the log has been running-only through the crossing and after. The most recent strength sessions showed the usual moderate, mostly-Z1 pattern with occasional climbs into higher zones on the more demanding days, consistent with functional-fitness circuits rather than steady cardio. Nothing in the sensor-source agreement stands out; the fallback estimates during the block track cleanly with the surrounding data and there's no divergence worth flagging.
sections.calendar: The calendar has gone from densely packed during the crossing to sparse over these two recovery days — a sharp compression followed by a gap, which mirrors the effort itself. This is still within the window where a gap reads as absorption rather than avoidance. The signal to watch is the return to the usual interleaved spread of running and strength; if the sparse patch extends much further, it starts to hint that recovery cost more than the low trail HR suggested.
sections.personal_bests: Nothing PB-relevant is in reach right now, and that's by design — the recent block was pure durability at slow controlled paces, the opposite end of the spectrum from the speed-based short-distance bests. Those bests remain from last autumn and sit untouched by this training focus. They'll come back into play only once faster sessions resume and the legs are clear of trail fatigue.

watch_items: Watch whether the first easy run back sits at normal HR for its pace, or runs elevated — the clearest read on whether the crossing is still being paid down.
Watch for strength to re-enter the log; its continued absence is now the most open thread from the block.
Watch whether the calendar returns to its usual interleaved rhythm rather than extending the current gap.
Watch whether sleep consolidates now that the block's short broken nights are behind you.
